framework.summary: Robotics adoption should be analysed by task structure and economic payback, not by humanoid form factor. The first large deployments are likely where environments are controlled, tasks repeat, labour cost is visible and safety certification is tractable.

waves.name: Structured logistics + fixed industrial automation
waves.whyFirst: Highest current ROI, repeatable environments, large existing installed bases and relatively low autonomy requirements.
waves.powerStackRead: Prefer suppliers with recurring software/service economics or cross-industry exposure over single-customer moonshots. This wave also increases demand for motors, drives, sensors, industrial networking and factory power infrastructure.

waves.name: Cobots + mobile manipulation + constrained service robots
waves.whySecond: AI perception and better foundation models expand the task set without requiring full human-level dexterity. Deployments can still be bounded by geofencing, known workflows and human supervision.
waves.powerStackRead: This is likely the best bridge from conventional automation into Physical AI. Watch utilisation, task-success rates and customer payback rather than demo quality.

waves.name: Humanoids in factories and warehouses
waves.timing: Third / pilots now, meaningful scale later
waves.whyThird: Human-shaped environments create a theoretical advantage, but dexterity, reliability, battery life, safety and cost remain harder than deploying purpose-built machines.
waves.powerStackRead: Treat humanoid OEMs as high-duration venture-style equities until there is evidence of paid deployments, repeat orders, high utilisation and acceptable total cost of ownership. Component suppliers may monetise earlier.

waves.name: Open-world consumer and general-purpose robots
waves.whyFirst: Lowest near-term confidence because messy environments, safety liability, edge cases and consumer price sensitivity compound the technical difficulty.
waves.powerStackRead: Avoid paying today for a mass-market outcome that still requires major reliability and cost breakthroughs.

ideas.name: Symbotic
ideas.thesis: One of the clearest public-market exposures to the first robotics adoption wave: high-throughput warehouse automation with measurable customer economics rather than general-purpose humanoid optionality.
ideas.catalysts: More systems entering deployment, margin expansion, new verticals and autonomous-forklift integration following Fox Robotics.
ideas.risks: Customer concentration, execution on complex deployments, lumpy revenue and valuation sensitivity.
ideas.valuationTechnical: Fundamentals are improving faster than many speculative robotics peers, but the stock can still rerate violently around deployment timing. Prefer accumulation on execution-backed pullbacks rather than chasing robotics-theme spikes.
ideas.researchNote: Q2 FY2026 revenue was $676m, up 23% YoY, adjusted EBITDA reached $78m and systems in deployment rose to 70. This is the strongest pure-play candidate in the current US robotics scan.

ideas.name: Geekplus
ideas.thesis: Direct listed exposure to warehouse AMRs, where robotics adoption is already commercial and task environments are structured.
ideas.catalysts: International warehouse automation demand, order conversion, embodied-intelligence improvements and continued margin discipline.
ideas.risks: China valuation volatility, competition, project cyclicality and customer capex sensitivity.
ideas.valuationTechnical: More investable than pre-profit humanoid stories because the company has crossed into adjusted profitability, but still deserves a growth-stock rather than industrial-multiple framework.
ideas.researchNote: 2025 revenue rose 31.6% to RMB3.171bn, orders rose 31.7% to RMB4.137bn and adjusted net profit plus operating cash flow turned positive.

ideas.name: Cognex
ideas.thesis: Machine vision is a form-factor-agnostic bottleneck for robots and automated production lines. It can win whether the end machine is a conventional arm, AMR, cobot or humanoid.
ideas.catalysts: Factory automation recovery, electronics/logistics investment and higher machine-vision content per automated line.
ideas.risks: Industrial cyclicality, electronics/customer concentration and premium quality multiple.
ideas.valuationTechnical: Prefer on industrial-cycle weakness. The attraction is lower dependence on any one robot architecture than an OEM bet.
ideas.researchNote: Differentiated enabler exposure; arguably a better Power Stack fit than chasing every humanoid manufacturer.

ideas.name: Teradyne
ideas.theme: Cobots + autonomous mobile robots + semiconductor test
ideas.thesis: Universal Robots and MiR give Teradyne exposure to cobots and mobile robots while semiconductor test provides a second earnings engine tied to AI compute.
ideas.catalysts: Cobot adoption, mobile-robot recovery and AI/data-centre semiconductor test demand.
ideas.risks: Robotics is diluted by the larger test business, semiconductor cyclicality and competitive industrial automation markets.
ideas.valuationTechnical: Useful crossover rather than a pure robotics bet. The dual AI-test plus physical-automation exposure deserves a premium only if both businesses are executing.
ideas.researchNote: Good bridge between the existing AI stack and Physical AI, but not as clean a robotics expression as SYM or Geekplus.

ideas.name: UBTECH Robotics
ideas.thesis: One of the more direct listed humanoid exposures, with industrial deployments providing a better starting use case than consumer-home robotics.
ideas.catalysts: Paid Walker deployments, repeat industrial orders, manufacturing scale and falling unit costs.
ideas.risks: Cash burn, high hardware cost, uncertain utilisation economics, intense Chinese competition and hype-driven valuation.
ideas.valuationTechnical: Do not value it like a mature automation company. Require evidence of repeat commercial orders and improving unit economics before raising conviction.
ideas.researchNote: Keep as the high-beta Hong Kong humanoid sleeve, not a core robotics holding.

ideas.name: Serve Robotics
ideas.thesis: Real fleet deployment gives Serve more evidence than many concept-stage robotics names, but current economics do not yet justify treating scale as proven.
ideas.catalysts: Higher utilisation, DoorDash/merchant diversification, hospital robotics expansion and improving per-robot economics.
ideas.risks: Q2 revenue miss, lowered 2026 outlook, cash burn, dependence on delivery volumes, public-space edge cases and dilution.
ideas.valuationTechnical: Deployment count is not enough; revenue and utilisation need to catch up. Keep below core-watch conviction until economics improve.
ideas.researchNote: More than 2,000 robots have been deployed, but the latest quarter weakened the near-term commercial case. Interesting technology, weak current risk/reward versus warehouse automation.

ideas.name: SoftBank Group ADR
ideas.theme: Physical AI platform + ABB Robotics acquisition
ideas.thesis: SoftBank is building a Physical AI portfolio and agreed to acquire ABB's robotics business for $5.375bn, creating exposure to an established industrial robot installed base plus AI optionality.
ideas.catalysts: ABB Robotics closing, integration with SoftBank AI assets and broader automation demand.
ideas.risks: Conglomerate dilution, acquisition execution, capital allocation and exposure to unrelated technology holdings.
ideas.valuationTechnical: Robotics is strategically important but not yet a clean enough earnings driver to justify a pure-play robotics valuation.
ideas.researchNote: Useful platform exposure; less useful if the goal is clean robotics beta.

notPromoted.name: Unitree
notPromoted.reason: Commercial progress is real, but the August 2026 Shanghai IPO is priced at an extreme multiple and remains outside the preferred HK/MY/US market set. Keep as a sector benchmark rather than a Power Stack core idea.

notPromoted.name: General-purpose home humanoids
notPromoted.reason: Too early for a high-conviction public-equity thesis. Reliability, safety, dexterity and total cost of ownership are not yet sufficiently de-risked.
